newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Hundreds sick with hepatitis in Russia's Far East.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds sick with hepatitis in Russia's Far East.

text.p: About 340 people have been taken to hospital with hepatitis in Russia's Far East over the last few days after drinking tap water on the Pacific island of Sakhalin, a state health official in Moscow said on Monday.
Galina Lazikova, told Reuters the outbreak of hepatitis A started in a district adjoining Patience Bay had been caused by badly-filtered water from a local river.

"The spring thaw has apparently brought the infection to the city. Those who did not boil tap water were infected," she said. Lazikova added that the outbreak was quite serious but the number of potential victims was confined to one district.
Hepatitis A is a viral inflammation of the liver that causes fever and sickness but is not usually fatal.
Interfax news agency quoted local epidemiologists as saying a military base up the river was to blame as it had been dumping waste into the river.
"With low-quality water filtering and disease spreading through human waste, anyone upriver could send the infection down, not necessarily the military," Lazikova said.
About 70 soldiers in Moscow were taken to hospital with hepatitis last week, also after drinking tap water at their army base.
